name: std::unexpect_t, std::unexpect
intro:
1) A tag type for in-place construction of an unexpected value in an std::expected object.

2) A constant of type const std::unexpect_t which is usually directly passed to a constructor of std::expected to construct an unexpected value.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: Like other construction tag types, unexpect_t is a trivial, empty class with an explicit default constructor.

examples.title: Practical use case
examples.input: Run the self-contained program; assertions check the documented behavior.
